---
title: "Maintaining Participant Attention"
description: "Approaches for maintaining fixation and attention during FPVS stimulation."
---

While FPVS is a passive method that does not require active participation from the participant to elicit neural responses, it is still important to ensure that the participant is paying attention to the stimuli being presented. If the participant does not fix their gaze on the screen during a study, the resulting neural responses would likely be meaningless or difficult to interpret.

[One common approach](https://doi.org/10.1167/15.1.18){target="_blank"} to maintaining the participant's attention is to ask the participant to fix their gaze on a small cross in the center of the screen and to press a button whenever that cross changes colors. This task is unrelated to the stimuli being presented on screen, but it ensures that the participant is paying attention to the screen.

```{=html}
<figure class="attention-task-demo" data-attention-demo>
  <div class="attention-task-screen attention-task-screen-square" role="img" aria-label="Blue fixation cross centered on a black display. The cross briefly changes to red at random intervals.">
    <span class="attention-fixation-cross" data-attention-target aria-hidden="true">+</span>
  </div>
  <figcaption>
    The fixation cross briefly changes from blue to red at random intervals.
  </figcaption>
</figure>
```

[Another approach](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0010945224000327?via%3Dihub){target="_blank"} is to include bars around the edges of the screen that change colors at random intervals, and similarly, to ask the participant to press a button whenever they notice a color change.

```{=html}
<figure class="attention-task-demo" data-attention-demo>
  <div class="attention-task-screen attention-task-screen-square" role="img" aria-label="A blue fixation cross remains centered between two blue vertical bars near the left and right edges of a black square display. Both bars briefly change to red together at random intervals while the cross remains blue.">
    <span class="attention-edge-bar attention-edge-bar-left" data-attention-target aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="attention-fixation-cross" aria-hidden="true">+</span>
    <span class="attention-edge-bar attention-edge-bar-right" data-attention-target aria-hidden="true"></span>
  </div>
  <figcaption>
    Following the linked study, two vertical bars briefly turn red at the same time while the central fixation cross remains blue.
  </figcaption>
</figure>

<script src="../assets/js/attention-task-demos.js" defer></script>
```
